title: Composition stability
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $h:Y\to Z$ be proper morphisms of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $\mathrm{IA}(f)$ and $\mathrm{IA}(h)$ hold in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property] (that is, $\mathrm{IA}_r$ for every prime $r$), then $hf$ is proper, $\mathrm{IA}(hf)$ holds, and hence $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$ holds in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-property].

proof.text: *Properness.* $hf$ is proper as a composite of proper morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], so $\mathrm{IA}(hf)$ and $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$ are defined [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property], [def-weil-pbc-property].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), statement ('proper morphisms'); Morphisms, Lemma 01W3 (label morphisms-lemma-composition-proper)

proof.text: *The squares.* Fix a prime $r$ and a base change $c:Z'\to Z$, with a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] for $hf$: a scheme $X'$ with $a:X'\to X$, $e:X'\to Z'$, $hfa=ce$, and $(X',a,e)$ a fibre product of $hf$ and $c$. Let $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $b:Y'\to Y$, $h':Y'\to Z'$; the square $(h,h',c,b)$ is cartesian. By the universal property of $Y'$ applied to $fa:X'\to Y$ and $e:X'\to Z'$ (which satisfy $h(fa)=ce$) there is a unique $f':X'\to Y'$ with $bf'=fa$ and $h'f'=e$. In the diagram formed by the upper square $(f,f',b,a)$ over the cartesian lower square $(h,h',c,b)$ the outer rectangle is the given cartesian square $(hf,e=h'f',c,a)$, so by the pasting lemma [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the upper square is cartesian: $X'=Z'\times_ZX=Y'\times_YX$. Both squares are cartesian squares in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with the identifications given by these fibre-product structures.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), proof, second paragraph ('set $Y'=Z'\times_ZY$ and $X'=Z'\times_ZX=Y'\times_YX$'); the pasting is Categories, Lemma 001Y, proof

proof.text: *$f_*I$ is injective.* Let $I$ be an injective sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$. The direct image $f_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] carries $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaves to $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaves and is right adjoint to the exact inverse image $f^{-1}$ on them [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], applied in the category of $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaves, $f_*I$ is an injective sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), proof, first paragraph (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0730, label sites-cohomology-lemma-pushforward-injective-flat)

proof.text: *Acyclicity along $f'$.* $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property], applied to the base change $b:Y'\to Y$ with the cartesian square $(f,f',b,a)$ of step 2 and to the injective $I$, gives $R^qf'_*a^{-1}I=0$ for $q>0$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), proof, second paragraph ('we know that $R^qf'_*a^{-1}\mathcal I$ ... are zero for $q>0$')

proof.text: *Underived exchange.* $I$ is killed by $r$, so it is a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] (every local section is killed by $r$). Since $f$ is proper and the square $(f,f',b,a)$ is cartesian, [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange] gives an isomorphism $b^{-1}f_*I\xrightarrow{\sim}f'_*a^{-1}I$ of abelian sheaves on $Y'_{\Et}$. (That node asks $f$ proper and the sheaf torsion; Stacks' Lemma 0A3U needs only $f$ proper; injectivity of $I$ is not used here.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), proof, second paragraph ('By Lemma 0A3U we have $b^{-1}f_*\mathcal I=f'_*a^{-1}\mathcal I$'); Lemma 0A3U (label lemma-proper-base-change-f-star)

proof.text: *Acyclicity along $h'$.* $\mathrm{IA}_r(h)$ [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property], applied to the base change $c:Z'\to Z$ with the cartesian square $(h,h',c,b)$ and to the injective $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf $f_*I$ of step 3, gives $R^ph'_*b^{-1}f_*I=0$ for $p>0$. Since $R^ph'_*$ is a functor, the isomorphism of step 5 gives $R^ph'_*(f'_*a^{-1}I)\cong R^ph'_*(b^{-1}f_*I)=0$ for $p>0$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), proof, second paragraph ('$R^q(g')_*b^{-1}f_*\mathcal I$ are zero for $q>0$')

proof.text: *The spectral sequence.* For $X'\xrightarrow{f'}Y'\xrightarrow{h'}Z'$ and the abelian sheaf $a^{-1}I$ on $X'_{\Et}$, [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence] gives a first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=R^ph'_*R^qf'_*a^{-1}I\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(h'f')_*a^{-1}I$, converging in the sense of [def-sp-convergence]. Let $n>0$ and $p+q=n$, $p,q\ge0$. If $q>0$, then $R^qf'_*a^{-1}I=0$ by step 4, so $E_2^{p,q}=R^ph'_*(0)=0$. If $q=0$, then $p=n>0$ and $E_2^{p,0}=R^ph'_*(f'_*a^{-1}I)=0$ by step 6. Each $E_\infty^{p,q}$ is a subquotient of $E_2^{p,q}$, hence $0$ for $p+q=n$. Convergence of a first-quadrant spectral sequence gives a finite filtration $0=F^{n+1}\subseteq F^n\subseteq\dots\subseteq F^0=R^n(h'f')_*a^{-1}I$ with $F^p/F^{p+1}\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}=0$, so by descending induction every $F^p$ is $0$ and $R^n(h'f')_*a^{-1}I=0$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), proof, second paragraph ('Using the spectral sequence (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0734) ... we conclude that $R^p(g'\circ f')_*a^{-1}\mathcal I=0$ for $p>0$'); the degeneration argument is written out here

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Since $h'f'=e$ is the base change of $hf$ along $c$ in the given cartesian square, and $r$, $c$, the square and $I$ were arbitrary, step 7 is $\mathrm{IA}_r(hf)$ for every prime $r$, i.e. $\mathrm{IA}(hf)$ [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property]. As $hf$ is proper (step 1), [lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity] (direction 2 $\Rightarrow$ 1) gives $\mathrm{PBC}(hf)$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), proof, first paragraph ('We will use the equivalence of Lemma 0A4B without further mention'); Lemma 0A4B (label lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives)

split_report.summary: Rewritten from Stacks Etale Cohomology Lemma 0A4D (lemma-composition), the composition step of 0A4F; the imported one-paragraph proof is split into 8 steps. Statement: 'proper' repointed from def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions to def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-pbc-property added to stmt_deps (PBC is in the statement), properness of hf made explicit. Steps: properness of hf (lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition, tool of sk-thm-br, as already accepted on lem-weil-pbc-reduction-projective-space); construction of Y'=Y x_Z Z' and f' with the top square cartesian by the pasting lemma (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting, CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_vert_iff) - the import silently assumed the base-changed squares; f_*I injective in F_r-module sheaves (lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives, whose statement names only 'etale sheaves'); IA_r(f) along b; underived exchange (lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange needs f proper and the sheaf torsion: I is killed by r; injectivity not needed); IA_r(h) along c on f_*I; Grothendieck spectral sequence for h'f' with the degeneration written out (E_2 vanishes in positive total degree, finite filtration of the abutment); conclusion IA(hf) and PBC(hf) via lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity (now in uses; it was in proof_deps only). def-weil-pbc-property is no longer a proof use beyond step 1. All R^q are those of def-weil-pbc-direct-image (abelian sheaves), consistently with def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property.
